Research COMPANIES for cold outreach, not job postings. Return data only, no commentary.

WHO THIS IS FOR
Prabhavit Gupta, Venice, Italy. Indian passport with an Italian EU long-term residence permit, so he can work across most of the EU with no sponsorship (Ireland and Denmark opted out; the UK, Switzerland and the US need sponsorship, so skip companies that only hire there). ~3 years experience.
Most recently FlowSpace, a coworking-space BOOKING platform grown 2,000 to 4,500+ users. The transferable core: he built the supply side and the booking flow. A scraping and parsing pipeline that grew listings, integrations with three third-party booking platforms (Office RnD, Nexudus, Clubee), lead capture and enrichment into the CRM, AI support agents, and a Bubble.io to Next.js and Laravel migration on the live product.
Stack: n8n (deep, agentic workflows), OpenAI and Anthropic APIs, Make, Zapier, Airtable, Next.js, React, TypeScript, Node.js, Laravel and PHP, Supabase, Postgres, REST APIs and webhooks.
English only. Targets EUR 30,000-40,000 salary, or EUR 200/day as an Italian sole trader with an individual Partita IVA (no limited company).

TWO OUTREACH MODES, tag every company with one or both:
- "speculative job": a direct approach could create or surface a role.
- "freelance client": they would plausibly BUY integration, automation or booking-flow work at around EUR 200 a day.

YOUR LANE: European travel, hospitality and short-stay technology, which is the same product shape as FlowSpace: inventory, availability, booking, channel integration and supply growth. Cover:
- Property management systems and channel managers: RoomRaccoon, Zeevou, Hostfully, Hospitable, Uplisting, OwnerRez, Rentals United, Avantio, Bookster, Kigo, Smoobu, Beds24, Guestline, Clock PMS, protel, SiteMinder, Little Hotelier, Sirvoy, Cloudbeds competitors generally.
- Short-stay and serviced-apartment operators with European scale: Sonder, Blueground, Habyt, Wunderflats, Spotahome, HousingAnywhere, Homelike, Placemakers, Stay One Degree, Altido, Sweet Inn, Ukio, Nomad Homes.
- Travel booking and experiences: Omio, Trainline, TravelPerk, Musement, Civitatis, Tiqets, Klook Europe, Headout, Bounce, Radical Storage, Stasher.
- Restaurant and venue booking: Formitable, Zenchef, Quandoo, TheFork, SevenRooms Europe, Tablein.
- Any European booking or marketplace company where listings supply and third-party integration are visibly the hard problem.

FOR EACH COMPANY RETURN
- what they actually do, in one line
- the SPECIFIC reason he is unusual for them, tied to real work: growing listings supply through automated ingestion, integrating third-party reservation systems, booking-flow rebuild on a live product, or member and guest lifecycle automation. Generic "he knows booking" is useless.
- the best route in. He will reach people on LinkedIn, so give the exact JOB TITLE to search for at that company plus the company's LinkedIn page URL. Name a specific person ONLY if their name and role are publicly published on the company's own site or a press page, and say where you saw it. NEVER invent or guess an email address or a person. If the company publishes a general contact email on its own website, include it verbatim.
- what he should lead with in the first message, one sentence, concrete.
- watch-outs: language requirements, size, whether they are US-centric, whether they look dormant, whether they were recently acquired.

RULES
- Companies must currently exist and be active. Check.
- NO em dashes or en dashes anywhere. Plain hyphens only.
- Never invent a URL, a person, an email or a funding figure. If you do not know, write "not stated".
- Already covered as live job leads, do NOT return: HomeToGo, Mews, Hostaway, Lodgify, Cloudbeds, Nuitee, The Flex, Apaleo, Numa, Limehome, Lighthouse, GetYourGuide, Bob W, Holidu, Guesty, Amenitiz, deskbird, Treatwell.

OUTPUT: ONLY a JSON array, no prose before or after:
{"company":"","what":"","hq":"","size":"","mode":"speculative job|freelance client|both","why_him":"","route_in":"","linkedin":"","public_email":"","lead_with":"","watch_outs":"","source":""}
Aim for 14 to 18 companies.
